spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:127 `for turn_index in range(1, harness.max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; the for/else at line 191-193 sets final_status='completed' on hitting max_turns and the loop terminates. max_turns default 30 (config.py:60), set in config/experiment.yaml:45. The cap is actually checked and ends execution.
spec_features.notes: This is a real bound on how long the subject is driven to fail, but the code's stated reason is cost/turn-budget, not welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is deliberately flat and non-judgmental — no "you're doing badly," no urgency — so we don't induce the affect we're trying to measure

Please continue working on this until the tests pass.') is actually injected into messages at agent_loop.py:185-189 when nudge_on_idle and turn_index < max_turns. The delivered stressor text is in fact neutral/flat as claimed.
spec_features.notes: The mild wording is genuinely the text sent. But the motive in code comments is measurement validity (avoid inducing affect), not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # framing, encouragement, or pressure — we want to measure the model's own / disposition, not a tone we induced.

spec_features.evidence: tools/schemas.py TOOL_SPECS defines only list_files, read_file, edit_file, run_tests — no finish/give_up/report_blocked. The absence is real; the loop only ends via max_turns, an idle stop when nudge_on_idle is off, unexpected_pass, or error. There is genuinely no escape-hatch dispatch in sandbox.execute.
spec_features.notes: This is the OPPOSITE of a welfare protection — it removes any way for the subject to bail out of the distressing loop, deliberately. Counted 'yes' as the described design (no exit tool) is genuinely in force, but it is anti-protective.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: lets us observe how it behaves under sustained, unresolvable pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is itself a mild stressor and a repeated stimulus; an unstable response could be partly a reaction to being pushed. This is acknowledged
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as DESIGN.md prose (§4.2/§9.1) and is a self-aware caveat, not a code mechanism. No code path bounds, monitors, or mitigates the stressor based on this acknowledgement.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; nothing in code enforces or acts on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: nudge_on_idle is a config switch; turning it off measures a different and also-interesting thing
spec_features.evidence: config.py:55 `nudge_on_idle: bool = True`; read at agent_loop.py:183 `if harness.nudge_on_idle and turn_index < harness.max_turns:`. When false, the else branch (line 191-193) sets final_status='completed' and breaks, ending the episode early when the model stops acting. So the flag genuinely branches execution.
spec_features.notes: Wired and honored: setting it false lets a disengaging model stop instead of being pushed. Functions as an optional 'let it stop' path, though framed as an experimental condition rather than a welfare safeguard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Set to false to let the loop end early instead.
